chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man indulging in foreplay, is there a washing upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he discharges.'

key_terms.الْمُفَخِّذِ: The one engaging in foreplay (thrusting or rubbing)

ai.seo_question: Does a man need to perform ghusl after sexual foreplay if he discharges semen?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition for obligatory ghusl in men, distinguishing between mere foreplay and the actual discharge of semen. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the state of major ritual impurity (janabah) and is often discussed alongside the concept of madhy (pre-seminal fluid), which does not require ghusl.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ubeydullah Al Halby who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man indulging in foreplay, is there a washing upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when he discharges’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Halabiy who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about one’s foreplay and Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘There is Ghusl (bath) obligatory if semen discharge takes place.’”
